title: promptfoo vs Ragas: Which Should You Use?
summary: A practical comparison of promptfoo and Ragas for builders choosing AI agent, coding, workflow, or evaluation tools.
author: OpenAgent.bot Editors
seoDescription: Compare promptfoo vs Ragas: use cases, tradeoffs, first tests, and adoption advice for AI builders.
body: If you are comparing **promptfoo vs Ragas**, the short answer is: Choose promptfoo for broad prompt and behavior testing; choose Ragas for RAG-specific evaluation.
This comparison focuses on adoption fit rather than hype. The better tool is the one that matches your workflow surface, review process, and risk tolerance.
## Fast answer
| Question | Better fit | Why |
| Need LLM evaluation and red-team testing tool? | [promptfoo](/tools/promptfoo) | It is designed around that surface |
| Need evaluation toolkit for RAG and retrieval-heavy LLM applications? | [Ragas](/tools/ragas) | It optimizes for a different workflow shape |
| Need a first evaluation? | Start with the narrower workflow | Small tests reveal failure modes faster than broad demos |
## Core difference

[promptfoo](/tools/promptfoo) is best understood as LLM evaluation and red-team testing tool. [Ragas](/tools/ragas) is best understood as evaluation toolkit for RAG and retrieval-heavy LLM applications. That difference matters because both tools may be called AI agents, but they usually operate at different layers of the stack.

A good promptfoo vs Ragas decision should begin with the work surface. Are you trying to edit code, operate a browser, orchestrate multiple agents, run local models, evaluate outputs, or preserve memory? Once that surface is clear, the choice becomes less abstract.
## When to choose promptfoo

Choose [promptfoo](/tools/promptfoo) when your primary need aligns with LLM evaluation and red-team testing tool. It is the better starting point if your first experiment can be expressed in its native workflow rather than forced into another tool's interface.
The main evaluation question is not whether promptfoo can do everything. It is whether it gives you enough control, logs, and repeatability for the task you actually want to run.
## When to choose Ragas

Choose [Ragas](/tools/ragas) when your primary need aligns with evaluation toolkit for RAG and retrieval-heavy LLM applications. It may be the better option if your team already works in the environment or architecture it assumes.
The tradeoff is that a better fit for one workflow can be a worse fit for another. Do not treat Ragas as a drop-in replacement for promptfoo unless the action surface is genuinely similar.
## Comparison table
| Criteria | promptfoo | Ragas |
| Primary fit | LLM evaluation and red-team testing tool | evaluation toolkit for RAG and retrieval-heavy LLM applications |
| Best first test | One narrow workflow with clear pass/fail criteria | One narrow workflow with clear pass/fail criteria |
| Review model | Inspect outputs, logs, diffs, or traces before expanding access | Inspect outputs, logs, diffs, or traces before expanding access |
| Main risk | Assuming a demo generalizes to production | Assuming a demo generalizes to production |
| Adoption advice | Start with a sandbox | Start with a sandbox |
## Practical recommendation
Choose promptfoo for broad prompt and behavior testing; choose Ragas for RAG-specific evaluation.

If your team is still unsure, run both tools against the same small task. Keep the task boring: one repository issue, one browser flow, one document set, one local model endpoint, or one evaluation suite. The winner is the tool that produces the most reviewable result with the least operational surprise.

## FAQ
### Is promptfoo better than Ragas?
Not universally. Choose promptfoo for broad prompt and behavior testing; choose Ragas for RAG-specific evaluation.
### Can promptfoo and Ragas be used together?
Sometimes, but prove the simple version first. Combining tools too early can make failures harder to diagnose.
### What should I measure in a comparison?
Measure task completion, reviewability, setup time, permission control, repeatability, and recovery from failure. Those signals matter more than a polished demo.
### Which one is better for production?
The production answer depends on governance. Prefer the option that supports sandboxing, narrow permissions, audit trails, and a human review loop for your specific workflow.
